blocks.text: India is the **world's most populous country (~1.4 billion)**. Its population is **unevenly distributed** — dense in fertile plains, sparse in mountains/deserts — and its **growth** is decelerating as India passes through the **demographic transition** (Census 2011 basis).

rows: Dense — Ganga plains, coasts, deltas; sparse — Himalayas, Thar, NE hills.
**Decadal growth 17.7% (2001-11)** — declining; TFR now below replacement (~2.0).

items: Density 382/km² (Bihar highest); decadal growth 17.7% (2001-11); UP most populous state.
Distribution driven by relief, rainfall, soil, water, urbanisation.

prelimsPointers: India's population (2011) — **1.21 billion**; density **382/km²**.
**Bihar** — highest density (1106); **Arunachal Pradesh** — lowest.
**Uttar Pradesh** — most populous state; **Sikkim** — least populous state.
**Decadal growth (2001-11) = 17.7%** — the sharpest-ever decline in growth rate.
Population is dense in **fertile river plains & deltas**, sparse in **mountains, deserts**.
**AP density ~308/km²** — below national average.
India became the **world's most populous country (~2023)**, overtaking China.
mainsAngles: Analyse the factors governing the distribution and density of India's population.

glossary.definition: The number of persons per square km; India's is 382 (2011).
The percentage change in population over ten years between censuses.
The shift from high to low birth and death rates as a society develops.

blocks.text: Population composition — **sex ratio, literacy and the occupational (work) structure** — reveals the quality and character of the workforce. India shows an **improving but adverse sex ratio, rising literacy, and a still-large but shrinking primary-sector workforce** (Census 2011).

rows: **Primary (agriculture) ~cultivators+labourers largest share; secondary (industry); tertiary (services) rising**; main vs marginal workers.

items: Sex ratio 943 (Kerala highest, Haryana lowest); literacy 74% (Kerala highest, Bihar lowest).
Occupational shift: primary → tertiary; AP sex ratio (~993) is favourable.

prelimsPointers: India sex ratio (2011) — **943**; **Kerala highest (1084)**, **Haryana lowest (879)**.
**Child sex ratio (0-6) = 919** — a worrying decline.
Literacy — **74%** (male 82.1%, female 65.5%); **Kerala** most literate, **Bihar** least.
**AP sex ratio ~993** (favourable); AP literacy ~67% (below national).
Workers classified as **main (>183 days)** and **marginal**.
Occupational structure — largest share still in the **primary sector (agriculture)**; **tertiary** rising.
'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' targets the adverse child sex ratio.
mainsAngles: Discuss the sex ratio, literacy and occupational structure of India's population.

glossary.definition: The number of females per 1000 males; India's was 943 in 2011.
Females per 1000 males in the 0-6 age group, a sensitive indicator of gender bias.
The distribution of workers across the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors.

blocks.text: India's population includes large **Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST)** communities and remains **majority rural**, though **urbanisation is rising**. These components shape welfare policy and India's social geography (Census 2011).

rows: **~16.6%** of population; highest share **Punjab**; listed under **Article 341**.
**~8.6%**; highest share **Mizoram/Lakshadweep**; most in absolute terms **MP**; **Article 342**.
SC ~17%, ST ~5-6%; ~70% rural; agency (tribal) areas in the Eastern Ghats.

items: Punjab highest SC share; MP most STs (absolute); AP ~70% rural.

prelimsPointers: **SCs ~16.6%** (2011); notified under **Article 341**; **Punjab** has the highest SC proportion.
**STs ~8.6%**; notified under **Article 342**; **Madhya Pradesh** has the most STs (absolute); **Mizoram/Lakshadweep** highest share.
STs live largely in the **'agency'/Scheduled (Fifth Schedule)** areas.
**PVTGs** (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups) — most marginalised tribes (e.g. Chenchu in AP).
Urbanisation is fastest in the southern & western states.
mainsAngles: Discuss the SC/ST composition and the rural-urban structure of India's population.

glossary.definition: Communities notified under Article 341 for affirmative-action protection.
Communities notified under Article 342, largely inhabiting Scheduled (agency) areas.
Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group — the most marginalised tribes (e.g. Chenchu).

blocks.text: India is an **extraordinary mosaic of races, tribes, religions and languages** — a **'unity in diversity'**. Its people are a deep intermixture; **Hinduism is the majority religion**; and it has **22 scheduled languages** across four major families.

rows: **22** in the 8th Schedule; most-spoken **Hindi**; **Telugu** among the largest Dravidian.
**~700+ Scheduled Tribes**; Gonds, Bhils, Santhals largest; AP — Koya, Chenchu, Savara.
Old typologies (Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Nordic) — of historical interest only.

items: Religion shares (Hindu 79.8%, Muslim 14.2%); 22 scheduled languages; 4 language families.
Treat 'race' cautiously (outdated). AP: Telugu + agency tribes.

prelimsPointers: Religion (2011) — **Hindu 79.8%, Muslim 14.2%, Christian 2.3%, Sikh 1.7%, Buddhist 0.7%, Jain 0.4%**.
Four language families — **Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic (Munda), Tibeto-Burman**.
**22 scheduled languages** (8th Schedule); **Hindi** most-spoken; **Telugu** a major Dravidian language.
India has **700+ Scheduled Tribes**; largest — **Gond, Bhil, Santhal**.
AP tribes — **Koya, Konda Reddi, Chenchu (PVTG), Savara, Yerukula, Lambada**.
Older **racial classifications** (Risley/Guha) are now considered obsolete.
'Unity in diversity' is the defining feature of Indian society.
mainsAngles: Describe the religious and linguistic diversity of India.

glossary.definition: The constitutional schedule listing India's 22 official 'scheduled' languages.
A group of related languages (India has four: Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic, Tibeto-Burman).
The idea that India's many races, faiths and tongues coexist within one nation.

blocks.text: **Urbanisation** — the rising share of people in towns and cities — is transforming India, driven by **migration** for jobs and services, and producing large **metropolitan regions**. It brings economic opportunity alongside challenges of slums, congestion and services.

rows: **31.2% urban (2011)**, rising; class-I cities & million-plus cities growing fastest.
**Rural→urban (dominant), urban→urban, inter/intra-state, international**; causes — economic pull, distress push.
**Million-plus cities**; mega-cities (>10 m) — Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata; census towns rising.
**Slums, congestion, water/sanitation, pollution, informal sector**; AMRUT/Smart Cities respond.
Urbanising around **Visakhapatnam (largest), Vijayawada-Guntur (capital region)**; loss of Hyderabad (2014).

items: 31.2% urban (2011); rural-urban migration dominant; mega-cities >10 million.
Challenges: slums/services; AP urbanises around Vizag & Vijayawada-Guntur.

prelimsPointers: India is **31.2% urban (2011)** and rising.
**Rural-to-urban** is the dominant internal migration stream; driven by **economic pull & agrarian push**.
**Mega-cities (>10 million)** — Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata; **million-plus cities** the fastest-growing.
Migration classified as **intra-state, inter-state and international**; marriage & work are top reasons.
Urban challenges — **slums, congestion, sanitation, pollution, informal employment**.
Programmes — **Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, PMAY (Urban)**.
**AP** urbanises around **Visakhapatnam** & the **Vijayawada-Guntur** capital region.
mainsAngles: Examine the causes and consequences of urbanisation and migration in India.

glossary.definition: The increasing proportion of population living in urban areas.
A large city and its surrounding urbanised area functioning as one unit.
A settlement with urban characteristics not yet formally municipal, a driver of India's urban growth.
